name: Old State House
heritage: National Historic Landmark; National Register of Historic Places listed place; Boston Landmark
text: The Old State House (originally the Second Town-House; also the Court House, Province House, or Old Provincial State House) is a historic building at 206 Washington Street in Boston, Massachusetts, United States. Completed in 1713, it is the city's oldest extant public building, hosting the judicial, legislative, and executive branches of the Massachusetts provincial and state governments during the 18th century. At 65 feet (20 meters), it was also the tallest building in Boston until 1745.

depictions.text: Old State House (Boston) The Old State House is a building in Boston that historically housed Massachusetts' colonial and, later, state legislature from 1713 to 1798.
